subject: Meridian pilot: acceptance latch, exit gates, and decision protocol
summary: Drafted a compact set of success anchors, 'stoplight' exit gates, and ownership for acceptance tests for Meridian's pilot. Agreed next steps: finalize MAP spreadsheet, align on 3 blocking tests, schedule executive sign-off on Feb 19.
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ken Robinson <krob@consultco.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot acceptance criteria — Meridian / Redwood

Hi Stephanie / Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Meridian's triage team liked the latency and hallucination safeguards. Procurement asked us to put down a concise acceptance list and any hard exit gates before we sign the SOW. Can you share the MAP-style list of success metrics and the specific acceptance tests you plan to run during the 6-week pilot?

High-level asks from Meridian:
- A short list (3–5) of non-negotiable tests we can include in the SOW
- Clear pass/fail thresholds and rollback triggers
- Owners for each test and expected dates for artifacts (logs, smoke reports)

Ken (our integrator) will help scope integration tests; procurement included in CC for timelines.

Appreciate a compact doc we can attach to the SOW.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Triage Operations
Meridian Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ken Robinson <krob@consultco.com>, procurement@meridianhealth.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance criteria — Meridian / Redwood

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a compact MAP workbook (meridian_map_v1.xlsx) and a one-page acceptance test plan (pilot-acceptance-tests.md). Below is the suggested minimal set of acceptance anchors and the stoplight exit gates we'd recommend including in the SOW.

Acceptance anchors (3 required to pass):
1) Latency P50/P95: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 400ms for 99th percentile of customer traffic shape (measured across week-long samples).
2) Accuracy/concordance: Mean response-level concordance >= 92% against Meridian gold prompts (50-sample daily evals).
3) Safety filters: Zero critical PHI exfiltration incidents during 14-day smoke (automated scanner + manual spot checks).

Stoplight exit gates (fail fast):
- RED (block production): any single critical PHI leak confirmed by manual review; sustained P95 > 800ms for 48 hours; or average concordance < 85% on two successive daily runs.
- YELLOW (remediation path): intermittent P95 spikes between 400–800ms, or concordance 85–92% — requires mitigation plan + 72-hour follow-up run.
- GREEN (go): anchors met for rolling 7-day window and smoke artifacts uploaded.

Acceptance tests (owners & artifacts):
- Latency smoke (Owner: Marcus Lin) — synthetic replay of production-like traces, artifact: latency histogram + raw traces (expected by week 2).
- Concordance eval (Owner: Soojin Lee) — blind sampling against Meridian gold set, artifact: confusion matrix + sample pass/fail list (week 3 cadence).
- Data-handling / PHI safeties (Owner: Soojin Lee) — automated filter test + manual spot reviews, artifact: scanner logs + review notes (day 7 and at cutover).

We recommend embedding these as discrete line items in the SOW so procurement can use them as objective acceptance triggers. I attached the MAP workbook; Marcus and I will update the timeline column after Marcus confirms resource dates.

Next steps:
- Marcus: confirm runtime test window and tooling (by Tue 16 Feb)
- Soojin: confirm gold set size and sampling cadence (by Tue 16 Feb)
- Redwood / Meridian exec sign-off meeting: propose Fri 19 Feb 10:00 PT

Thanks — happy to iterate on thresholds if your team prefers different risk tolerances.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0189

Attachments: meridian_map_v1.xlsx, pilot-acceptance-tests.md

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ken Robinson <krob@consultco.com>, procurement@meridianhealth.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance criteria — Meridian / Redwood

Thanks — quick notes from runtime perspective:
- We can run latency smoke against a 48-hour replay window starting Day 3 of the pilot. I'll own the job and push artifacts to the shared Drive.
- For P95 SLA measurement: we'll use contiguous 1-minute buckets to avoid sampling noise. If P95 breaches RED, we'll automatically shift traffic to the staged fallback pool (per MAP).
- Infrastructure caveat: to simulate peak traffic shape we need a 2-hour burst window scheduled; Ken, can you confirm endpoint tokens for that run?

Proposed updated timeline in the MAP workbook (high-level):
- Week 0: MAP sign-off, credentials exchange, baseline run
- Week 1–2: Latency smoke + safety scan
- Week 3–4: Concordance longer-run and iteration tuning
- Week 5–6: Final stability window + executive review

I'll update meridian_map_v1.xlsx with the job owners and exact run dates this afternoon.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@meridianhealth.ai>
Cc: Ken Robinson <krob@consultco.com>, procurement@meridianhealth.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance criteria — Meridian / Redwood

Quick confirmation and one refinement before sign-off:
- Gold set size: propose 250 prompts covering triage common+edge cases; we'll report daily 50-sample concordance but keep the 250-sample sweep for week 3 and week 6 verification.
- Failure mode for concordance: recommended immediate rollback (RED) only if we see systematic category failures (e.g., hallucinations leading to unsafe instructions) across >=10% of samples in the 250-sweep. Is Meridian comfortable with this threshold?

I also attached a short security snapshot (security_snapshot.pdf) that lists the logs and retention policies we'll provide for audit. For procurement: the MAP will be included as Appendix A in the SOW; please confirm if you need more formal wording for the remediation SLA window (we used 72 hours for YELLOW fixes).

If Meridian agrees, we can lock the MAP and I will publish the pilot-acceptance-tests.md as the canonical artifact. Proposed sign-off meeting remains Fri 19 Feb 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Staff Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: security_snapshot.pdf
